analysis: Examined three changes. (1) docs/reports/README.md adds one index link (head line 7) to a new dated measurement report; it changes no controls or behavior and adds no trust claim. The linked report file is not in the supplied evidence, so its contents were not reviewed. (2) libs/mlx-swift-lm is a submodule pointer bump from 0351444e to cef66217. The submodule diff is not supplied, so inference-engine changes (TB-007, T-041 cache, T-028 residual GPU data, T-029 idle timeout, and the decrypted-prompt handling it touches) are unreviewed. The README text mentions a 2,048/4,096 prompt geometry and a Gemma 4 media ceiling, which suggests prefill chunk and step-budget and media-limit changes in the engine. That is a coverage limit, not evidence of a defect. (3) The SchedulerPrefillBenchmark.swift patch is partial; only the schema version bump to 5 and the new optional prefillChunkTokens and maxBatchedTokensPerStep fields are visible. This is a benchmark-only tool outside the coordinator, provider, and authorization paths. The fields are optional Codable, so older receipts still decode. No handling of secrets, keys, attestation, or network input is visible. The visible benchmark and doc changes do not touch TB-002, TB-011, T-053, or the fan helper. Open question for integration: the submodule bump could alter the memory admission, prefill geometry, media size limits, or prefix-cache storage behavior (T-041, T-050) in the production provider. The pointer change should be reviewed against the mlx-swift-lm commit range.
